newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish oil tanker burns on in Istanbul dock.
newsitem.headline: Turkish oil tanker burns on in Istanbul dock.

text.p: Firemen battled a blaze on board a docked Turkish oil tanker for the third day running on Saturday and officials said the fire was close to being extinguished.
Anatolian news agency quoted Istanbul fire brigade chief Muhittin Sogukoglu as saying the flames had been contained to the 159,982-tonne TPAO-Istanbul's own fuel depot.
Twenty-seven people, 19 of them firemen, have been injured in the fire which started on Thursday with an explosion on the vessel, docked at Tuzla in Istanbul province.

The TPAO-Istanbul is Turkey's biggest oil tanker, built in 1977 and owned by state maritime company Ditas. It was in the yard for repairs for eight days. Dockyard officials say it will probably now be scrapped.
Nobody was injured in a large explosion on the ship on Friday that was captured live on television.
